verdict.line: You win if you deny Nasus's Siphoning Strike stacks early and dive him under turret off your level-6 Stormbringer, and you lose if the lane stalls long enough for his stacks and eventual Fury of the Sands to outscale the lead you built.

brief.thesis: Nasus's entire power curve is gated behind Siphoning Strike (Q) landing killing blows on minions — deny those last hits and he is permanently behind. Volibear's Q (Thundering Smash) stun into W (Frenzied Maul) re-cast trades let him punish Nasus for stepping up to farm, which is why the data shows a lane and solo-kill edge for Volibear; but once Nasus banks enough stacks and reaches Fury of the Sands (R), the fight math flips, which is why the overall head-to-head sits at 46.7% over 184 games despite the early edge.

theirWindow.when: Wither (W) off cooldown and you're in range
theirWindow.what: Once Wither lands it decelerates your movement and attack speed over time, which guts your Frenzied Maul re-cast trades and your Q stun gap-close. Back off or bait it before committing to an extended fight.

yourWindow.when: Nasus steps up to last-hit under his Q cooldown
yourWindow.what: Siphoning Strike only empowers him when it kills — walk him off the minion or punish the animation with Q (Thundering Smash) into immediate W trades before he can secure the stack.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: 72.5% pick at 49.2% win rate — the mana and health regen sustain repeated Q/W trade attempts without forcing a back before you've denied enough Siphoning Strike stacks.

boots.why: Highest measured win rate of the two options (60.7%) and the slow-resist built into Swiftness directly blunts Wither's deceleration, keeping you in range to land your own Q stun.

core.why: First item in the most-played core path — the attack speed and tech it provides feeds the passive's bonus magic damage proc during W-stacking trades.
Second in the 8.5%-pick core path — more attack speed pushes your Q-into-W trade window and keeps pace once Nasus's stacks start closing the gap.
Closes the core path and gives sustain through extended skirmishes once Nasus's Fury of the Sands drain starts chunking max health.

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramps attack speed into extended trades, stacking with your passive's attack speed grant to accelerate the bonus magic damage proc and win prolonged fights against Nasus's Wither.

summoners.why: Dominant pick at 81.6% and a 50% win rate — Ignite converts your solo-kill advantage into actual kills and cuts through Nasus's Soul Eater lifesteal sustain during early all-ins.

playing.title: Deny Siphoning Strike stacks
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike only empowers Nasus's future Qs when it lands a killing blow. Walk him off minions with Q (Thundering Smash) into W (Frenzied Maul) before his Q timer comes back around.

playing.title: Trade only when Wither is down
playing.detail: Wither (15-11s cooldown, 700 range) decelerates your movement and attack speed over time. Track it and only commit to extended trades or dives in the window after it's used.

playing.title: Zone Spirit Fire with E
playing.detail: Sky Splitter (1200 range, 16s cooldown) can punish Nasus for standing in his own armor-reducing Spirit Fire patch, and its slow sets up a follow-up Q stun.

playing.title: Dive under turret at level 6
playing.detail: Stormbringer disables nearby enemy towers on landing. Press the level-6 spike immediately and all-in Nasus under his own plates before his stacks matter.

playing.title: Always re-cast W for the heal
playing.detail: Frenzied Maul's second cast on a marked target deals bonus damage and heals you — use it in every trade to offset his Soul Eater lifesteal.

playing.title: Bait empty Siphoning Strikes
playing.detail: Stand just past 255 range while his Q is up to bait a whiff, denying the stack and gold while opening him up for your own W trade.

playing.title: Respect Fury of the Sands late
playing.detail: Once his R is online he gains bonus health, range, and max-health drain. Don't extend solo skirmishes against him past mid-game without your Q stun pre-planned.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the win-rate framing and tactical reasoning — stack denial, Wither timing, and the level-6 turret dive — are my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus grow during early game by applying pressure to win lane control. Use [E] to contest lane and after reaching level 6 dive under turret.
